about: What an applicant can choose to build, the idea-to-move-in timeline per pathway, recommended steps, and where to escalate. LAW and SKIPPED entries cite data/sources/index.json. ASSUMPTION entries are the event brief's typical estimates (starter repo, lanes/2-clear-it/data/timeline.json), not measurements. drawMonths is only for drawing bar lengths. Written by Giuseppi's session.

paths.label: Backyard home to rent
paths.fact: No owner-occupant requirement. The city may only require rentals of 30 days or longer.

paths.label: Backyard home to sell
paths.fact: Selling an ADU on its own is a special case: the Handbook refers to sale to a qualified buyer under Gov Code 66341. We have not checked 66341 yet.

paths.label: Duplex or lot split (SB 9)
paths.fact: The city must approve an urban lot split parcel map ministerially (no hearing) if it meets SB 9's criteria.

ADU.text: Submit the application. The city has 15 business days to tell you in writing if it is complete.
Expect approval or denial within 60 days of a complete application, with no hearing.
Use state-approved or pre-approved plans where the city offers them.

SB9.text: Check the lot meets SB 9's eligibility criteria before you apply.
Ask the city for its SB 9 review time in writing. We have not sourced a deadline.
Start on land that is already zoned for what you want to build.

escalation.handles: Requests for technical assistance when a city's handling conflicts with state housing law. HCD's 2026 letter to Orange began with such a request from an applicant's consultant.
